input: What has Salesforce changed in Agentforce pricing in 2026?

output.answer: As of November 10, 2026, Salesforce has expanded Agentforce beyond a single consumption model: it introduced a standalone Agentforce Coworker license at $50 per user per month, and its current pricing page offers Flex Credits at $500 per 100,000 credits, Conversations at $2 per conversation, and Help Agent resolutions at $2 each. In September, Salesforce replaced the prior enterprise tiers with Core ($195/user/month), Advanced ($395), and Max ($550); Core, Advanced, and Max include 500,000, 1 million, and 2.75 million Flex Credits respectively, while Max stayed at the former Agentforce 1 price and existing Agentforce 1 customers can upgrade at no extra cost. Salesforce also launched outcome-based Help Agent pricing in July: customers pay only when the agent autonomously resolves an issue, with no charge for escalation or an unsuccessful interaction.
caveats: Salesforce says pricing and packaging are subject to change, availability can vary by region, and customer agreements govern final pricing.
The current pricing page does not provide a publication date; its listed prices are treated as current as of 2026-11-10.
Salesforce's September announcement says new Industry Edition pricing would take effect later in fall 2026, but the opened sources did not verify a separate Industry Edition price or effective date.

output.question: What has Salesforce changed in Agentforce pricing in 2026?

key_facts.fact: Salesforce introduced Agentforce Coworker as a standalone license priced at $50 per user per month; the SKU was available in November 2026.
Salesforce's current Agentforce pricing page lists Flex Credits at $500 per 100,000 credits, Conversations at $2 per conversation, and Help Agent Resolutions at $2.
Salesforce introduced Core, Advanced, and Max editions at $195, $395, and $550 per user per month, respectively.

The new editions include 500,000 Flex Credits for Core, 1 million for Advanced, and 2.75 million for Max; Max had no price increase versus Agentforce 1, and existing Agentforce 1 customers could upgrade at no extra cost.

Agentforce Help Agent introduced pay-per-resolution pricing: customers are charged only when it autonomously resolves an issue from start to finish, and not when the customer escalates or is dissatisfied; the pricing became available in July 2026.
